inline_comments.comment: Per project rules, `code/core/src/manager/globals/exports.ts` is **auto-generated** by `code/core/scripts/generate-source-files.ts` and must not be manually edited — changes will be overwritten on the next codegen run. All four new entries (`announce`, `clearAnnouncer`, `destroyAnnouncer`, `toHaveLiveRegion`) should be picked up automatically once `code/core/src/components/index.ts` exports them; run the generator script to regenerate this file rather than hand-editing it.

`toHaveLiveRegion` is a Vitest custom matcher — a test-only utility. Globalizing it in the production manager runtime is inappropriate: it ships test-assertion code to end users and expands the manager's runtime surface with a symbol that has no meaning outside of tests. The other three additions (`announce`, `clearAnnouncer`, `destroyAnnouncer`) are legitimate runtime functions. The stories already register the matcher locally via `expect.extend({ toHaveLiveRegion })` at module scope (line 17 of the stories file), which is the correct place for it. Remove `toHaveLiveRegion` from this globals list and rely on the per-file `expect.extend` call in stories.

The JSDoc says **"string for exact match"** but the implementation on line 60 uses `content.includes(text)`, which is a **substring** match. A string like `'Tests passed'` will match an element whose `textContent` is `'3 Tests passed, 0 failed'`. Either change the JSDoc to say "substring match" or tighten the implementation to use `content === text` (or `content.trim() === text`) for true exact matching. Exact matching is usually safer for announcement assertions to prevent false positives.

general_comments.comment: The PR description claims `extend-to-be-announced` was added as a devDependency in `code/core/package.json` and registered in `code/.storybook/storybook.setup.ts` via `import 'extend-to-be-announced/vitest'`, but neither is present in the diff. The actual implementation uses a hand-rolled `toHaveLiveRegion` DOM-inspection matcher instead. The custom matcher checks whether an `aria-live` element with the expected text **currently exists in the DOM**, but `@react-aria/live-announcer` clears its live-region content after a short delay. This means the test window is narrow and relies on timing. `extend-to-be-announced` captures announcements at the moment they are made (via `MutationObserver`) and makes them available regardless of subsequent DOM cleanup — which is a fundamentally more reliable approach for testing announcements. If `extend-to-be-announced` was intentionally dropped, the PR description should be updated and the architectural trade-off documented.

The `toHaveLiveRegion` test utility is exported from `storybook/internal/components` (a production bundle). Test-only matchers add unnecessary bytes to the components bundle shipped to every Storybook user. Consider moving `toHaveLiveRegion` and `LiveRegionMatcherOptions` to a dedicated testing-utilities entry point (e.g., `storybook/internal/test-utils`) so they can be tree-shaken from production builds.

`code/core/src/components/components/LiveRegion/LiveRegion.tsx` contains no JSX — it is purely a re-export barrel. The `.tsx` extension is misleading; rename it to `LiveRegion.ts` to correctly signal that it contains no markup.
